basis: Nails-only dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa causes nail dystrophy or absence without blistering or other organ disease.
Fluoride accumulation causes metabolic bone disease with osteosclerosis, joint impairment and ligament calcification.
REEP6-related rod-cone degeneration is confined to the retina and associated ocular structures.
Organic aciduria, cardiomyopathy and cerebellar ataxia define DCMA; anemia occurs in 12/18. Hepatic steatosis and optic atrophy are below 30%.
Inherited organic acid metabolism disorder; no consistent organ-damaging phenotype. Reported neurologic abnormalities are occasional.
Developmental disability defines the syndrome. Retinal dystrophy 80-99%; renal defects/CKD and aganglionic megacolon 30-79%; obesity omitted under the four-axis cap.
Name indicates congenital autonomic vagal reflex dysfunction; no definition or phenotype evidence establishes additional organ damage.
Benign neoplasm arising in kidney tissue or the renal pelvis.
Inherited cutaneous lupus/interferonopathy causes persistent acral inflammatory skin lesions; common extracutaneous damage is not established.
Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disease of myeloid blood cells and bone marrow; the translocation adds no organ axis.
Umbrella of peroxisomal oxidative enzyme/protein defects; affected organs differ substantially among its subtypes.
Menstrual cycle-dependent febrile syndrome; fever alone establishes neither immune disease nor organ damage. Cortisol elevation is occasional.
Inherited progressive skin pigmentation disorder; oral pigmentation does not establish gastrointestinal injury or impaired function.
Premalignant epithelial dysplasia of the uterine cervix is confined to a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Peroxisome biogenesis defect; developmental delay/spastic paraplegia, nephrocalcinosis and cataract each reported in 1/1 patient; frequency evidence is limited.
Open spinal neural-tube defect with vertebral spina bifida and Chiari II malformation; lasting secondary urinary tract damage is not established in >=30%.
Visceral bacterial infection most commonly occupies the lungs; liver, spleen, kidney and brain involvement is described without evidence of >=30% frequency.
LOX-related thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection; reported skeletal, ocular and skin abnormalities are below 30%.
Congenital gonadotropin deficiency defines the disorder; developmental olfactory dysfunction with anosmia affects roughly half, in Kallmann forms.
HNRNPC-related developmental and intellectual disability; feeding difficulties and hypotonia do not establish separate gastrointestinal or muscle damage.
Congenital thumb aplasia/hypoplasia is a skeletal deformity; unspecified cardiovascular abnormalities lack frequency evidence.
Inherited coagulation defect causing APC resistance; venous thrombosis is a separately diagnosed complication rather than universal vascular damage.
Lethal skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia and cataract annotated at 80-99%. Coarctation omitted because 2/2 conflicts with its broader occasional annotation.
Cerebral arterial obstruction reduces brain perfusion and causes neurologic injury; both brain and cerebral vasculature define the disease.
Mitochondrial energy metabolism defect; neurologic dysfunction and skeletal myopathy each occur in roughly >=30% across clinical cohorts; other organs vary by subtype.
